title: I Took the Scuba-Tank Fill Log to the Tech Who Palmed My Air

parts.text: I rolled tank eight to the whip at 8:04 a.m. and tech Soren was already filling past our numbered ticket. The board said: ONE FILL. THREE THOUSAND. TICKET STAYS WITH THE TANK. I was thirty-five, club diver, holding a vis that listed our mix. Soren shrugged. "Techs are the air." I photographed the board, the ticket, and his whip on our valve. Then I asked for the fill log. At 8:12 the shop pinged why Soren's name was on our three thousand. I kept my voice shop-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A board is only a board until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop can see Soren's whip on our valve during our fill.

social.video_title: He filled past our numbered ticket on our tank — Part 1/2
social.description: Scuba shop, a tech on our valve, a fill log he posted. I logged the whip. Would you have asked for the fill log?

parts.text: Soren called it a top-off until the shop asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the whip still. The tank went back to our vis. Soren ran his own fill and told the next tech atmosphere was always about mix. Mix is a word techs use when a log exists. Fill policy now has a second line: TECHS ARE NOT THE AIR. I keep our tank on a labeled rack. Soren brown-bags his jokes. The shop finally looks like a fill, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Techs are not the air — Part 2/2
social.description: Fill log, numbered ticket, and a second line on the board. Was a top-off ever our valve?
